title: Zoomie: A Software-like Debugging Tool for FPGAs
problem: FPGA development workflows lack familiar debugging interfaces available in software development, making it difficult to inspect execution state and identify bugs. This debugging complexity creates a significant barrier to adopting agile development practices for FPGA-based projects.
motivation: FPGAs are critical for pre-silicon verification and datacenters acceleration, but development friction from inadequate debugging support prevents widespread adoption and agile methodologies.
method: Zoomie provides a debugging tool that replicates software debugger interfaces and workflows for FPGA development. It enables real-time execution inspection, breakpoint support, and hardware state visibility through familiar debugging paradigms to reduce the learning curve.
key_novelty: Bridging the usability gap between software and FPGA development by providing software-like debugging interfaces and workflows for hardware designs.
contributions: Software-like debugging interface for FPGAs enabling familiar debugging workflows
Real-time execution visibility and inspection capabilities for FPGA designs
Reduced barrier to entry for developers transitioning to FPGA development
Support for agile development practices in FPGA-based projects
